concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which of the following was the British East India Company's first major victory in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Battle of Plassey** took place on **23 June 1757** between the forces of the British East India Company led by **Robert Clive** and the Nawab of Bengal, **Siraj-ud-Daulah**. 
• The battle was fought near **Plassey**, located in present-day **West Bengal**, along the banks of the Bhagirathi River. 
• The British East India Company secured a decisive victory due to the betrayal by **Mir Jafar**, the commander of Siraj-ud-Daulah's army, who sided with the British. 
• This victory marked the beginning of **British political dominance** in India, as it paved the way for the establishment of British control over Bengal and later other parts of India. 
• The **Battle of Plassey** is widely regarded as the **first major victory** of the British East India Company in India, setting the foundation for their empire in the subcontinent. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Battle of Ambur:** 
• The **Battle of Ambur** was fought in **1749** between Anwaruddin Khan, the Nawab of Arcot, and the combined forces of Chanda Sahib and the French. 
• It marked the beginning of French involvement in Indian politics but was not a major victory for the British East India Company. 
• **Battle of Wandiwash:** 
• The **Battle of Wandiwash** took place in **1760** between the British and the French during the **Third Carnatic War**. 
• It was a significant victory for the British, leading to the end of French ambitions in India. However, this occurred after the Battle of Plassey. 
• **First Anglo-Maratha War:** 
• The **First Anglo-Maratha War** occurred between **1775 and 1782**. 
• The war ended with the Treaty of Salbai, and it was not a major victory for the British East India Company. 
• **Significance of the Battle of Plassey:** 
• The Battle of Plassey allowed the British East India Company to gain control of Bengal's immense **wealth** and resources, strengthening their position in India. 
• It led to the installation of **Mir Jafar** as the puppet Nawab of Bengal, ensuring British dominance in the region. 
• The revenue from Bengal helped the British finance their wars and expand their presence in other parts of India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Robert Clive:** 
• Robert Clive, often called "Clive of India," was the British commander who led the forces during the Battle of Plassey. 
• He played a crucial role in establishing British supremacy in India. 
• **Mir Jafar:** 
• Mir Jafar's betrayal of Siraj-ud-Daulah was instrumental in the British victory at Plassey. 
• He was later installed as the Nawab of Bengal but remained under British influence. 
• **Economic Impact:** 
• The victory at Plassey provided the British East India Company access to Bengal's **resources**, including its lucrative **trade routes** and **wealth**. 
• The Company began collecting **taxes directly** from Bengal, significantly boosting its financial strength. 
• **Political Impact:** 
• The battle marked the beginning of **British colonial rule** in India. 
• The Company's influence expanded from Bengal to other parts of India, eventually leading to the establishment of the British Empire in India. </ul
